lineage.strategy: Use the Groves startup-authorization execution record as a distinct build/commissioning capability signal, while explicitly avoiding inference that it resolves Aurora commercial licensing or economics.

observations.fact: DOE startup authorization allowed Oklo to load fuel, conduct startup testing and proceed toward first criticality at the Groves isotope test reactor after a build-and-authorization period of just over 10 months from groundbreaking.

Oklo states the Groves program required facility construction, operating-organization establishment, personnel qualification, nuclear programs/procedures, fuel and major-equipment procurement and DOE authorization, providing an observable integrated execution sequence.

risks.risk: Groves is a low-power isotope test reactor; its schedule and authorization pathway do not establish Aurora commercial power-plant licensing, construction cost, power economics or fleet scalability.

unknowns.unknown: Transferability of Groves execution learning to Aurora's larger commercial-power scope, economics and remaining regulatory path is not quantified.

recommendation: Use only as bounded evidence of integrated nuclear project execution capability; do not treat it as proof of Aurora commercial economics or final authorization.
